name: Division
shortDef: Assuming that what's true of the whole must be true of each of its parts.
definition: Concluding that a part or member has a property because the whole or group it belongs to has it. A top-ranked school, a winning team or a high average can still contain weak or struggling parts.
howToSpot: Is a trait of a group, team or total being pinned on one member?
Is an average or overall result treated as true of every individual?
Could the whole have the trait while some of its parts lack it?
classicExample: Ashford is a wealthy town, so everyone who lives there must be wealthy.
legitimateVersion: Some traits do pass from whole to parts, such as a recall covering a whole batch or a rule covering every unit. It's fair when the trait applies to each part by its nature or by definition.

contrast.fal_composition: Division goes from the whole down to its parts; composition goes from the parts up to the whole.
contrast.fal_hasty_generalization: Division assumes a part shares the group's overall trait; hasty generalization builds a claim about the group from too few members.
